What's more likely, all you observe is a lie, or one or, one or more of the assumptions you used to form this theory is flawed?

It's based on simple and easy to follow logic with minimal assumptions.

  • Evolution favors adaptions that are beneficial.
  • Your brain is a product of evolution.
  • Your brain chooses the world you 'see.'
  • Seeing the world in precise the "real" way is a subset of all possible ways to see the world.
  • The chances that the way you currently see the world is "real" approach 0.

You can give basic examples of this with things like vision. The entire electromagnetic spectrum ranges from wavelengths of a picometer (1 trillionth of 1 meter) up to low frequency radio waves which can have wavelengths in the millions of meters. In this entire spectrum all we can see is this fairly arbitrary range from 390 to 700 nanometers. There is nothing at all special about x-rays, infrared, microwaves, gamma rays, radio waves, or any of these things. The only reason we can't see them is because evolution decided these limited eyes were most optimal for the conditions we were in. It's not like visible light is actually visible. It's just another nondescript range on the electromagnetic spectrum that evolution decided we would be able to directly perceive. By comparison evolution granted birds the ability to see in ultraviolet and this is reflected on their coats which may look bland to our limited eyes yet quite varied and remarkable in uv light.

This doesn't directly lead to a false reality, but I do think it does directly lead to the fact that what we see is a very select and limited picture of reality chosen by the whims of evolution.
